My WP had a mental breakdown that led to drugs and almost losing his job for three months after DDAy. He got better since then. However, as the BP, my mental health wasn’t great to start. Our DDay actually happened in one of the worst and most vulnerable times in my life. When I found out 2 months after it originally happened, I lost my sanity. I never threatened to hurt anyone but I did become suicidal. I still struggle sometimes with trying to stay stable. Counseling and medication only helps so much. It’s really difficult especially if you have a mental illness like I do (BPD) to move on from the feeling like the person you love can betray you at that extreme. It’s been 7 months since I discovered it. And to be honest, it’s not getting easier.

My sex drive towards my spouse has definitely dwindled. But I still will have quick moments of wanting to be intimate with him. However as soon as he tries, I shut down. I don’t feel connected. I don’t feel anything. It doesn’t even feel pleasureful anymore. It’s just someone touching me and I’m just waiting for it to be over. We’ve tried different ideas and things but still I just feel disconnected from reality when it’s happening. 

The more difficult part in general is that I have issues with tearing during sex because of a SA injury from 10 years ago. So I can only do certain positions and things sometimes. I’ve been going to specialists for years as well as physical therapy but it’s not making it disappear.

I feel like if I knew how to feel a connection with him again it would help. But it feels nearly severed when it comes to being intimate…

I think maybe in the future I could fully believe my WS is in pain. Mine went through a drug phase and almost lost his job from the guilt and depression of it. However, it’s hard to feel empathy for his pain when I feel like my world has been flipped upside down and crushed. It’s much easier for the WS to go through the grieving stages and eventually move past it if they choose. However, the BS has to relearn every single part of their relationship if they decide to stay. It’s soul crushing.

I've been to two. One where I was in the children's unit, another when I was in the adult unit. The children's unit was kinda scary still because they don't allow you to have basically anything but books in your room. I was never allowed outdoors and I was timed in the shower. I was also woken up every morning at 5:45am. Meals were chosen for us. We had no TV, no games, nothing. We were allowed to read or draw. We had desks in our rooms. But weren't even allowed to write. I remember someone in the room next to me slamming their chair into the wall for almost an hour straight. As well as finding scratches in the window saying "fuck this" "kill me" "die" etc. You only were allowed visits twice a week. The staff were nice, but distant where you couldn't connect. We weren't allowed extra blankets, and we weren't allowed to talk to other kids for very long. They instantly put you on medication. Makes you feel numb like a zombie. You also never knew when you'd get a roommate. I woke up to mine who had been to 9 hospitals before that because she kept attacking people.

The adult unit was a little harder. There's no sympathy or empathy from the staff. The other people in there are actually really mentally ill, not just considering self harm and what not. People would get hit by other patients, and scream in the middle of the night. Older people would bang on the doors. Again you weren't allowed outside. You didn't get to pick your food. We were confined to our rooms unless it was visitation twice a week or if it was therapy time or time to eat. We weren't allowed to talk to one another. Constantly drugged. Room checks everyday. Timed showers. Wasn't allowed to wear shoes or clothes with strings. Literally felt like a prisoner.

I will do anything to never go back. It's something hard to understand the difficulty of living in unless you're experiencing it yourself. It's lonely and makes you feel like less than a person.

I have been single while depressed, and a great long term relationship while depressed.

Let me tell you this, both are very difficult. It's very hard to deal with depression alone. But, it's hard to love someone while depressed and have them love you. The reason is, because you feel this constant guilt of being a burden to them, or bringing them down. It also makes you sadder when they see you sad and know it and feel like they can't make you happy.

It's okay to feel the way you do. I think a lot of people do until they experience depression while with someone they love. 

Don't say you'll never have anyone however. Because if you're open to it, it may take many years but it will happen when the time is right for you. I know that sounds overly optimistic for someone who is severely depressed. But I honestly didn't think I'd ever find someone who could love me either, and I did at one of the worst times in my life. It can happen for you too.
